description: A single grouped (clustered) bar chart plotting inclusion size distribution for three steel samples; it is a conventional statistics plot, not a spectrum or micrograph. The vertical axis is labelled "Number percentage (%)" and is drawn from 0 to 70 with tick marks every 10 units. The horizontal axis is labelled "Size distribution (μm)" and carries three bins, printed as "1-5", "5-10" and ">10". A boxed legend in the upper-right corner maps three hatch patterns to the samples "1 #", "2 #" and "3 #" (fine diagonals, denser diagonals and cross-hatch respectively). Every bar carries a printed data label: in the 1-5 μm bin 58.4, 53.6 and 48.2%; in the 5-10 μm bin 32.3, 34.6 and 46.9%; in the >10 μm bin 9.4, 11.8 and 4.9%. Within each bin the bars run 1 #, 2 #, 3 # from left to right, so bar position tracks increasing Al content (1 → 3 → 5). The three values in a bin sum to approximately 100%, so the bins partition the whole measured inclusion population. The chart demonstrates that as Al content increases the fraction of small (1-5 μm) inclusions falls monotonically, the 5-10 μm fraction rises monotonically, while the >10 μm fraction rises from 1 # to 2 # and then drops sharply in 3 #. No error bars, absolute particle counts or measurement statistics are shown.

observations.observation: The figure is a grouped bar chart of inclusion number percentage versus inclusion size class for three samples, with no error bars and no absolute inclusion counts printed.
The y-axis is labelled 'Number percentage (%)' and is scaled from 0 to 70 with tick marks every 10; the x-axis is labelled 'Size distribution (μm)' with bins '1-5', '5-10' and '>10'.
The legend box in the upper right maps three hatch patterns to sample labels '1 #', '2 #' and '3 #'.
Printed data labels for the 1-5 μm bin are 58.4, 53.6 and 48.2 for samples 1 #, 2 #, 3 # in left-to-right order.
Printed data labels for the 5-10 μm bin are 32.3, 34.6 and 46.9 for samples 1 #, 2 #, 3 #.
Printed data labels for the >10 μm bin are 9.4, 11.8 and 4.9 for samples 1 #, 2 #, 3 #; the 4.9 bar is the shortest bar in the whole chart.
Within every size bin the three values sum to approximately 100%, indicating the three bins partition the whole counted inclusion population.
The caption states the figure shows the size distribution of inclusions in three samples.
The citing text states that inclusions sized 1-5 μm account for 58.4%, 53.6% and 48.2% of the total number in 1 # to 3 # samples, matching the printed labels.
The citing text states that inclusions sized 5-10 μm account for 32.3%, 34.6% and 46.9% of the total number in 1 # to 3 # samples.
The citing text states that inclusions larger than 10 μm account for 9.4%, 11.8% and 4.9% of the total number in 1 # to 3 # samples.

The citing text asserts that with increasing Al content the 1-5 μm fraction decreases, the 5-10 μm fraction increases, and the >10 μm fraction first increases then decreases; the bar ordering 1 #→2 #→3 # is what encodes that increasing Al content in the figure.
The largest bar in the chart is 58.4% for sample 1 # in the 1-5 μm bin, i.e. small inclusions dominate in every sample.
